newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico same-day Cetes rate up 175 bps to 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico same-day Cetes rate up 175 bps to 20 pct.

text.p: Same-day Cetes rates rose up to 175 basis points to reach levels of 20 percent as the Mexican peso plummeted against the dollar, traders said.

"There's still a hangover effect from what (Federal Reserve chairman Alan) Greenspan said yesterday, the dollar continues to rise very strongly and that is causing fears on the secondary market", one dealer said.
Traders said that if the peso continued to weaken, secondary market interest rates were likely to rise further.

As well as the Greenspan remarks, dealers said the money market had been hit by concerns that Mexico might not win full certification from Washington as an ally in the drug war. A decision on that issue is expected within the next 48 hours.
